title: Let the upload queue let go

blocks.text: The file service virus-scans every upload before storing it. Uploads wait in an `UploadQueue` that lives as long as the service; the scanner takes them one at a time, and an operator can discard everything still waiting. Each upload carries its whole body. After a busy morning the queue is empty, yet the heap stays near its limit, and the service later fails with `OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` in the PDF thumbnailer. A heap dump taken after the morning shows the morning's upload bodies, all reachable from `UploadQueue.items`.
`put(...)`, `size()` and the growth of the array are done. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/UploadQueue.java`:

items: `take()`: hand out the oldest waiting upload, or `null` when none is waiting;

blocks.text: When you're done, the queue keeps an upload in memory only while it is waiting, whether it left the queue by being scanned or by being discarded. About eight lines in total.
The tests ask the garbage collector for a full collection and check, with weak references, which upload bodies are still in memory.

cases.says: uploads come out oldest first, also after the queue wraps around and grows
discarding empties the queue, and it then takes and hands out new uploads
once every upload has been taken and scanned, the queue no longer keeps any of them in memory
discarded uploads are no longer kept in memory by the queue

origin.section: OutOfMemoryError Is Thrown by Whichever Allocation Fails, Not by the Code That Filled the Heap

concepts: A collection that is empty to its users but keeps references in slots it no longer reads keeps those objects reachable, so the collector can't free them.
